GS.rationale: Goldman Sachs shows strong fundamental health and positive trajectory. Q1 2026 revenue of $17.23B (+14.4% YoY) and EPS of $17.55 (+24.3% YoY) demonstrate robust earnings growth, with operating margins of 37.5% and net margins of 29.9% reflecting high profitability. The firm's ROE has improved to 14.7% (from 12% a year ago), and the balance sheet, while leveraged as expected for a G-SIB, shows total equity of $122.78B against $2.06T in assets. The strategic pivot back to core investment banking and markets is paying dividends—Q1 saw a hot M&A market with $1.2T in deals and investment banking revenue up 48%. The firm just passed the Fed stress test and announced an 11% dividend increase to $5.00/share, its 15th consecutive year of increases, signaling confidence. Valuation is moderately elevated vs. its own history: P/E of 17.4x sits near the top of its 14.5-18.9x 365-day range, and P/B of 2.56x is at the high end of 1.8-2.8x. This is not cheap, but the improved ROE and earnings trajectory partially justify the multiple expansion. A near-term catalyst exists: Q2 earnings on July 14, with consensus expecting $13.95 EPS (up from $10.91 YoY) and $15.9B revenue. The firm is also positioned to benefit from major upcoming IPOs (SpaceX, OpenAI, Anthropic). However, risks include: (1) operating cash flow was deeply negative at -$31.87B in Q1, typical for banks but worth monitoring; (2) the Fed now expects at least one rate hike in 2026, which historically correlates with market corrections; (3) CET1 ratio dropped to 12.5% due to aggressive buybacks; and (4) the stock has already rallied +18.7% in the past quarter, limiting upside. The score of +0.35 reflects solid fundamentals and a credible near-term catalyst, tempered by rich valuation and macro headwinds.

sources_cited.excerpt: Goldman plans to raise its dividend from $4.50 to $5 per share
Goldman Sachs raised its quarterly dividend by 11% to $5.00 per share after passing the Federal Reserve's stress test, marking the 15th consecutive year of dividend increases
Analysts expect quarterly earnings of $13.95 per share, up from $10.91 per share in the year-ago period. The consensus estimate for Goldman Sachs' quarterly revenue is $15.9 billion.

The Federal Reserve now expects at least one interest rate increase in 2026, reversing earlier expectations for rate cuts. Historical data shows that the previous four rate-increase cycles since 1999 coincided with stock market corrections
The bank's CET1 ratio dropped sharply to 12.5%, driven by aggressive share buybacks and balance sheet expansion
